title: The emergency unwind runbook terminates in burning USDS, prioritizing repayment of Sky over holding recovered cash
content:
The Emergency Protocol defines a three-step liquidation sequence, each step written as a total sweep rather than a sized action. First, recover positions: "in order to withdraw all ERC-4626 balances, the operator must call the `redeemERC4626` function" with `token.balanceOf(address(proxy))` (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.3.2.1). Second, consolidate: `swapUSDCToUSDS(usdc.balanceOf(address(proxy))` to "centralize all recovered liquidity in USDS" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.3.3). Third, repay: `burnUSDS(usds.balanceOf(address(proxy))` to "repay and then burn Pattern's USDS debt" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.3.4).

The ordering encodes a priority. The terminal state of an emergency is not Pattern holding a pile of stablecoins — it is Pattern's vault debt extinguished and its balance sheet collapsed back toward zero. Sky's exposure is retired before anything else is considered, which is consistent with the Liquidity Layer being a credit facility rather than the Agent's own treasury.

Writing each call against a live balance rather than a fixed amount is a deliberate operational choice: the runbook stays correct regardless of position size, and an operator under time pressure has no quantity to compute or mistype.

Note also what the sequence relies on: step two funnels through the PSM path, which the same document shows can require iterative `psm.fill` refills and can revert with "DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.6.2.1). The unwind is therefore dependent on PSM liquidity being available at the moment it is most likely to be strained.
description: Redeem ERC-4626 positions, swap all recovered USDC to USDS, then burn the Proxy's full USDS balance to wipe vault debt — each step specified as a balance-sweeping call.
